title: Find the thin-walled tube among three sealed look-alike cylinders with a two-lane roll race
instruction: The three grey cylinders with red, green and blue end bands look the same and weigh the same. One is a thin-walled tube, one a thick-walled tube and one a solid rod. Put the thin-walled tube in the red bin and leave the other two out of it. The orange button opens and closes the start gate at the top of the two-lane ramp.
context: Inspectors in receiving and quality control (O*NET 51-9061) sort round parts whose inside cannot be seen: capped and painted spacers, rollers and bar offcuts that are made to the same size and weight. A thin-walled tube passed on in place of a thick-walled tube or a solid rod buckles under a clamp or a bearing load. Here the parts are sealed and equal in mass, so looking and weighing do not tell them apart; how fast each one rolls does. Two lanes rank only two parts per race, so the robot has to plan the comparisons, keep the starts fair and bin the right one.
setup: Station table; positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), arm bases at y +-30.5. Two-lane roll-race track, plywood, clamped (20 kg in the simulation): a base board 23 cm wide (x 23.5 to 46.5) and 1.5 cm thick from y -20 to +26.2; a ramp plank at 15 degrees from its foot at y +2 to its top at y +25 (top surface 7.7 cm above the table) with an end board above the top; lanes painted at x 30 and x 40 with a 4 mm white line between them (no lane walls) and 1.2 cm PTFE-faced edge rails along both sides; an orange PTFE-faced start gate bar (23 x 0.6 x 2.2 cm) across both lanes at y +16 that drops 3 cm into a slot when opened; a flush black finish line (6 mm) at y -16; a catch pit from y -20 to -29 with a 3 mm blue foam floor 12 mm below the board and a 5 cm far wall faced with 6 mm foam. Gate button at (18, +30): dark 7 x 7 x 3 cm housing, orange 3.6 cm square cap with 8 mm travel; a press of 4 mm or more toggles the gate (closed at the start). Cradle rack at x 15 to 23, y -18 to +18: dark 4 mm base with four cradles of two rails (7 cm along x, 8 mm tall, 3.8 cm apart) at y +12, +2, -8 and -18. Three cylinders, loose, axes along x, in the cradles: red bands at (19, +12), green at (19, +2), blue at (19, -8); the cradle at y -18 is empty. Each is 50.0 mm across and 60 mm long, 211 g, painted the same grey (sRGB 158, 163, 173) over 2 mm ABS end caps, with a 10 mm band of red (217, 26, 26), green (26, 166, 51) or blue (31, 77, 217) vinyl tape at each end. One is a C360 brass tube (ID 44.2 mm), one a 6061 aluminium tube (bore 28.1 mm), one a solid G10 glass-epoxy rod, each body 56 mm long and 203 g. Red bin (sRGB 204, 20, 20), inside 10 x 10 cm, walls 3 cm tall, centred at (18, -30).
scoring: Score 0 if a cylinder falls off the table at any point, or if at the end any cylinder other than the thin-walled tube is in the red bin (centre inside the bin's inner walls, under 6 cm high, no gripper within 6 cm). Timed runs: when the button opens the closed gate, each cylinder resting behind it (centre within 2 cm of a lane centre and 8 cm uphill of the gate, axis within 3 degrees of square to the lane, under 5 cm/s, no gripper within 6 cm; at most one per lane) starts, and its time is from the gate opening to its centre crossing the finish line, within 4 s. A race shows A slower than B when A crosses more than 20 ms after B; solo runs show it when A's best time is more than 20 ms longer than B's; chains count. 0.5: the runs show the thin-walled tube slower than both other cylinders and no other cylinder is in the bin. 1.0 (success): that, with the thin-walled tube alone in the bin, released, and all three cylinders at rest for 1 s. Otherwise 0, including doing nothing, one race only, or binning without racing.
reset_notes: Close the gate. Put the cylinders back in their cradles, red at y +12, green at +2, blue at -8, axes along x; empty the bin. Between trials the operator swaps which tube or rod is under which colour band (bands are re-taped, or the three bodies are re-capped): the kind behind each colour is a random permutation per trial. Do not tap the cylinders.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies at 240 Hz. Each cylinder is one 50 mm, 211 g cylinder collider with inertia fixed at spawn from its material (I = k m r^2, k 0.88, 0.65, 0.50); each reset deals the bodies to the band colours by the seed. No rolling resistance, so times are ideal rolling (real parts lose a few percent, equally). The gate is a stiff sliding joint toggled in code by the button. Track, rack and bin rest on the table (clamped in a real build). A start counts only when squared within 3 degrees.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (4,800 steps, seed 0); scripted demo: 1.0 (seeds 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, 11)
